text.p: Top seed Alberto Costa of Spain came from behind to beat British-based German Kevin Goellner 6-7 6-2 6-2 in the final of the revived Bournemouth International Open on Sunday.
Compatriot Jose Higueras won the tournament the last time it was staged in 1983.
Costas finished a decisive winner in a mainly baseline duel but not before a protracted protest from Goellner in the fourth game of the final set.
Costa was leading 2-1 and 40-30 on the German's service and then hit a fierce forehand immediately called out by the line judge.
But umpire Gerry Armstrong over-ruled the decision, then awarded the game to Costa to give the Spaniard a crucial 3-1 lead.
Goellner demanded that the umpire look at the line. Armstrong came down from his chair but stuck to his decision.
Goellner appeared to lose heart and Costa, ranked 15th in the world, won three of the next four games to claim his third title of the year and a first prize of 36,000 pounds ($56,000).
